**Now built on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2)**, SST's latest release. 4.18.0 was built on 4.17.1. This release also fixes server routes next to prerendered pages, the visitor's address in SvelteKit apps, and JWT auth on WebSocket APIs.

### ⚠️ Before you upgrade

- **Node.js 22 or later is still required**, as since 4.18.0. The package now says so in its `engines` field: npm, pnpm and Bun warn when you install it on an older Node.js, and **Yarn 1 refuses to install it**. Upgrade Node.js everywhere you run `sst`, CI included.
- **An `ApiGatewayWebSocket` with JWT auth now stops at `sst diff` and `sst dev`**, not only at deploy. It could never deploy: API Gateway only supports JWT authorizers on HTTP APIs. Use a Lambda authorizer that verifies the token instead; the docs now show one. ([#51](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/51), [anomalyco/sst#6041](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6041))

### SST 4.17.2

SST 4.17.2 has one change, which guards a function's description in `sst dev` against a missing value ([anomalyco/sst#6984](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6984)). The fork has had the same fix since 4.17.3 ([#14](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/14)), so nothing changes for you. `sst version` now shows `built on SST 4.17.2`.

### Fixes

- **Server routes in a folder with prerendered pages no longer get a 403.** An `SsrSite` sent a whole asset folder to S3, so when a folder held a prerendered page, the server routes in it got S3's 403. In SvelteKit, a prerendered page or endpoint in such a folder could 403 too. Those folders' files are now listed one by one, so each request goes to S3 or to the server as it should. This applies to SvelteKit, SolidStart and Astro with a server. ([#35](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/35), [anomalyco/sst#6143](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6143))
- **`getClientAddress()` in a SvelteKit app returns the visitor's address behind CloudFront**, from `CloudFront-Viewer-Address`. It used to return CloudFront's own address, which changes from request to request, so rate limiting and logging saw the wrong address. It's in [`@sst-community/svelte-kit-sst`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sst-community/svelte-kit-sst) 3.0.1. The value can only be trusted when requests come through CloudFront: if you use it to allow or block clients, set `protection` on the `SvelteKit` component, or on the `Router` that serves it. ([#50](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/50))

### Changes

- **`ApiGatewayWebSocket` documents how to accept a JWT**, such as a Cognito token: a Lambda authorizer that verifies it with `aws-jwt-verify`. Its `jwt`, `payload` and `response` options are deprecated, since WebSocket APIs don't support or use them. ([#51](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/51))
- To update the SvelteKit adapter: `npm install svelte-kit-sst@npm:@sst-community/svelte-kit-sst@3.0.1`.

### Docs

- The landing page, the README and the docs intro say Node.js 22 or later is required.

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@4.18.1
```

To switch an existing project:

1. Check that `node --version` shows `v22` or later, wherever you run `sst`, CI included.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@4.18.1"` and reinstall.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. It still needs Node.js 22 or later, to run `sst.config.ts`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | bash
```
